kerberos.notes.keys: No key material is in this answer or on the page. A person's keys are derived from their password when it is set or verified and are never shown; a service principal's keytab is handed over ONCE, by the create or rotate that made it, and a person's keytab ONCE, derived from a password in hand — the one an administrator sets on the person's page, or their own on /portal/kerberos.
kerberos.notes.modeProduct: This KDC is a PRODUCT one: a person authenticates with their own password through the keys stored on their directory entry, and a person with none is refused with "sign in once".
kerberos.notes.modeDevelopment: This KDC is a DEVELOPMENT one: every user is keyed from krb5.userPassword and people are never given stored keys. Service principals created here are used in both modes.
kerberos.notes.realmServed: A KDC PER TRUST REALM: these are the people and applications of the trust realm this page is read in, as principals of its own Kerberos realm {{kerberosRealm}}.
kerberos.notes.realmNone: THIS TRUST REALM HAS NO KDC: {{reason}}. Set krb5.realm on the realm and turn krb5.enabled on to give it one; port 88 routes a request by the Kerberos realm name inside it.
kerberos.notes.realmInactive: THIS TRUST REALM'S KDC IS ON BUT CANNOT BE USED: {{reason}}. Its Kerberos realm is {{kerberosRealm}}.
kerberos.notes.window: Keys are derived AFTER a password is set or verified and take a few tens of milliseconds to land; until they do, the KDC refuses the person rather than accepting an older key.
kerberos.notes.previous: A password change or a rotation keeps the version it replaced — at most krb5.retainedKeyVersions of them, each for krb5.retainedKeyTtlS — so a ticket issued under it is still accepted until it could have expired. A previous version only ever OPENS such a ticket: nothing is issued under it and an old password never signs in. "Drop previous versions" ends the window at once, after a compromise.
